To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) there are no gender differences in single men’s and women’s migration patterns, (2) the migration behavior of egalitarian dual-earner couples is gender neutral, whereas (3) in traditional couples, men’s migration behavior statistically dominates that of women.

(1) single women and men have identical mobility patterns, (2) traditional couples migrate in response to male job-related characteristics, and (3) egalitarian couples are equally sensitive to male and female job-related characteristics.

(1) there is no gender gap in the geographic mobility of singles, (2) there is a significant gender gap in the migration of couples, and (3) the migration behavior of couples is driven by the division of housework.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relevance of gendered household structures for the geographic mobility decisions of families.
gender ideology, division of household labor and migration.

gender differences in migration behavior do exist, but only if gender ideology is taken into consideration and only for dual-earner couples.
gender ideology is a relevant factor in the migration behavior of couples, but that the relevance depends on the division of housework.
gender ideology is an important factor in the migration decision of dual-earner couples, and that the gender ideology of couples has to be measured by their division of household labor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
gender ideology is an important explanatory factor for migration behavior of couples.
the gender ideology of a couple matters for their inter-regional mobility, and the division of housework is a good proxy for this.
gender ideology matters for the geographic mobility patterns of dual-earner couples.
The main takeaway from our work is that

gender ideology matters for the inter-regional migration behavior of dual-earner couples, and it does so in the sense of a gender bias: egalitarian couples are more likely to migrate than traditional couples.
gender ideology is a key factor in the geographic mobility of couples and that the division of housework in dual-earner families can be a proxy for the degree to which the family is egalitarian.
gender ideology is a relevant determinant of the migration behavior of couples, and should be considered when analyzing family migration behavior.
